W1 (mechanism), after E013.

The setup
- The tip is E010: Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs (about 238 steps), and widths 128/384/512.
- It scores 6.639 s and 0.75477, a margin of 0.18 pp.
- E012 reran the tip bit-identically.
- E013 (label smoothing 0.3→0.2) gave +0.04 pp at −0.1% time. That is pure noise, so label smoothing is flat between 0.2 and 0.3.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time, deterministic (E003/E004, E010/E012).
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp at about 0.6% time (E005).
- LR floor 0.07→0: −0.08 pp. It is redundant with the EMA anneal (E009).
- Muon: +0.66 pp at +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time, −0.59 pp (E007).
- A 20 px stage: −0.97 pp. That is the resolution cliff: group-3 maps shrink to 2×2 (E011).
- 0.5 epoch cut: −0.18 pp, −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576→512: −0.25 pp, −4.8% time (E010).
- Label smoothing 0.3→0.2: about 0 (E013).

Time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: the host-to-GPU copy, the whitening eigendecomposition, the pad, the 25-way masked-copy augment with its host syncs, and the interpolate.
- The variable part is about 6.2 s, GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step.
- The Muon update is compiled with its lr as a GPU tensor. Fused SGD runs outside the compiled region, so its float lr causes no recompiles.
- Launch overhead is small next to roughly 26 ms of GPU work per step. CUDA graphs and graph-break removal are worth 0-3%, and mostly come from the augment syncs (0.1-0.2 s).
- Max-autotune with cudagraphs across 3 resolutions plus the optimizer state risks memory-pool and recapture costs, as in E003.

Accuracy model
- The averaging and optimizer changes (EMA, Muon) were larger than my priors. Hyperparameter retunes near the airbench values (LR floor, label smoothing) are flat.
- Muon renormalizes the conv weights and has no weight-decay term. So weight decay hits only the BatchNorm biases and the head; changing it moves accuracy by at most ±0.2 pp.
- Lookahead vs plain EMA: the alpha ramp gives an effective window of about 20 steps at the end. The reset also damps fast-weight variance during training.
- So a plain EMA probably keeps most of the endpoint-averaging gain but loses 0.1-0.5 pp.
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy:
  - epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% time;
  - width: about 0.5 pp per 10%;
  - moderate resizing: about 0.27 pp per 10%, with a cliff past it.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical per recipe; time repeats within 0.1-1%.
- Any kernel or RNG-path change reshuffles accuracy by about ±0.2 pp.
- Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- At 0.7548 the tip has about an 80-85% chance of a 40-seed mean of at least 0.75.

Unsure
- The held-out seed offset. E012 did not report it, and it decides whether the margin can be spent.
- The real size of the augment host stall under the 4-CPU pin.
- Whether a retune (Muon lr, warm-up length, momentum) hides +0.3 pp. The flat label-smoothing result lowers my prior that cheap retunes pay.
- The remaining levers are probably systems trims (about 2-4%), plus fine adjustments to epochs or resolution split if the seed offset is favorable.

forecasts.reason: The run is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step, so launch overhead is small; cudagraph capture across 3 resolutions plus the optimizer risks memory or recapture costs, so a ≥3% cut is unlikely.
Muon has no weight-decay term and renormalizes the conv weights, so halving wd touches only the BatchNorm biases and the head; nowhere near +0.3 pp.
Only the augment host syncs (0.1-0.2 s) are worth removing, about 2%; folding the augment into the compiled region changes the RNG path, so accuracy is not bit-identical.
Endpoint averaging keeps most of the gain, but losing the Lookahead reset raises fast-weight variance, probably costing 0.1-0.5 pp, which straddles the 0.3 pp threshold; likely falls below 0.753.

cruxes: What is the held-out (seeds 3-12) mean offset of the E010 tip? If it is at or above 0 pp, the margin is real and 0.25-0.5 epoch can be cut (about 2-5% time); if it is negative, the tip itself needs more epochs.
How much of the about 0.4 s fixed cost is the per-epoch masked-copy augment host stall under the 4-CPU pin, which sets the ceiling for systems-only gains?
Does Muon lr or warm-up length hide +0.3 pp of accuracy per epoch, which is the only non-systems lever left to buy back time?
